title: Fab assets or AI-generated 3D models for a UE game, which is more cost effective?
author: dnr424
selftext:
Planning to develop a game in Unreal and trying to figure out the asset side before I start. Fab stuff looks solid but buying enough of them for a whole game gets expensive. AI tools like Meshy and Tripo are affordable, but I hear the cleanup takes forever.

Anyone tried both? Is AI still cheaper once you count your time fixing it up, or do you mix the two?

comments.author: tindalos
comments.body: Why don’t you purchase a couple of good generic assets, then use ai to break them down and adjust pieces of them to make different people, cars, etc whatever

comments.author: Witty-Tangerine3606
comments.body: I had the same issue Fab assets are more expensive but better quality than AI generated. Still I didn't want to spend that much money on single assets so I built my own tool [FormFromLight](https://formfromlight.com/) it works well I am building 3 games at the same time with the MCP of formfromlight (you can connect it to claude or codex source: [FormFormLight MCP](https://formfromlight.com/docs/mcp)

comments.author: LupaStudioDev
comments.body:
I'd go with both tbh. Fab is great for modular environments, and Tripo is really handy for custom props.

Sometimes you spend way too much time fixing AI assets, and sometimes the AI just won't cooperate lol. But it's getting better pretty fast.

I just use whatever saves me more time.

comments.author: Patient-Software-168
comments.body: I use a local comfy ui 3d model workflow that I really like.

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body: Care to share the models you use? I tried trellis 2, works great for getting high poly model, but only that. Now I like using tripo + claude inside 3D software to further fix the topology till the asset is finished. Then I used RizomUVs for pretty much instant UVs, then substance designer/painter to get the textures done..

replies.author: Patient-Software-168
replies.body:
I also use trellis, but there are many workflows out there that affects the quality of the models.

A workflow can still change how trellis makes the models

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body: Ok, I'll give it another go then. Care to throw me a bone with any tips? 😅

replies.author: Patient-Software-168
replies.body:
[https://www.youtube.com/@PixelArtistry\_/videos](https://www.youtube.com/@PixelArtistry_/videos) this guy has so many workflows which I really enjoy. I can try to find out which workflow I use later.

Is it optimized for 5000+ tri models which fits my game well, but you can also get higher with good results

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body: Nice, thank you! 5k polygons per asset sounds good enough. I did follow this guy when I got kimodo installed

comments.author: teejayaiartdirector
comments.body: Claude is very good at making procedural models at this point, and Unreal Engine support procedural. It's worth looking into! 🔥

comments.author: Bullingju0
comments.body: I had Claude/ make some SVG files, those seem to come out pretty nice in Godot, at least for characters.
